articles.title: ‘Skintown’ Review: A Breezy, Loved-Up, Drugged-Up Guide to Getting Into Trouble in The Troubles
articles.summary: Nostalgia, like ecstasy, is a hell of a drug and Kieron J. Walsh’s warm-hearted, hot-headed “Skintown” is buzzing on both. A more polite brother to the “Kneecap” boys and a more cautious cousin to those “Derry Girls” still, the Fermanagh-set friendship comedy sends fizzy, sweetly chemical energy…
body: Against the backdrop of the 1994 IRA ceasefire, two friends land a score that could buy their ticket out of Northern Ireland in Kieron J. Walsh's Edinburgh Film Festival-winning charmer.

Still, as soon as Vinny gets the money together, he’s resolved to leave, although there are things he’ll miss: his supportive, hardworking paramedic mum (Roisin Gallagher); his peppy unrequited crush Eileen (Jamie Lee O’Donnell); and most of all, his best mate Jonty (Chris Walley), a shell-suited, high-spirited raver just out to have a good time. Vinny and Jonty are as thick as the thieves they eventually, inadvertently become when they’re pressganged into a caper involving a load of ecstasy stolen from the UVF (a loyalist paramilitary group).

articles.title: Venice-Bound ‘Meteorite,’ Debut Feature From Colombia’s Sebastián Múnera, Acquired by MoreThan Films (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: MoreThan Films has acquired Colombian filmmaker Sebastián Múnera’s film “Meteorite,” which will have its world premiere in Venice Critics’ Week (Sept. 2-12). The film follows Tefa and Nia, who live in a small town near the Magdalena River, where they raise Nia’s young nephew.
body: MoreThan Films has acquired Colombian filmmaker Sebastián Múnera ‘s film “Meteorite,” which will have its world premiere in Venice Critics’ Week (Sept. 2-12).

Queralt Pons Serra, managing partner at MoreThan Films, said, “What excited us about ‘Meteorite’ from the beginning was the strength and singularity of Sebastián’s gaze. You can really feel his artistic background in the way he approaches images, spaces and textures, creating a world that is incredibly cinematic, beautiful and also deeply emotional. There is something very immersive and atmospheric about the film that stayed with us long after watching it.”

Múnera is a Colombian visual artist and filmmaker. He was a resident at the Cité Internationale des Arts in Paris, invited by the Centre Georges Pompidou. His films have been selected at festivals such as IFFR Rotterdam, DOK Leipzig and FICCI Cartagena. He has received distinctions including the Humberto Solás Cine en Construcción Award and the International Symposium on Auteur Cinema Altiplano Incuba Award.
“Meteorite,” his first fiction feature, was awarded at work-in-progress programs in Málaga and Cartagena.

articles.title: Upendra Joins Cast as Teja Sajja, Shanaya Kapoor, Suparn S. Varma’s Sequel Titled ‘Zombie Reddy Nxt Lvl’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Kannada cinema superstar Upendra has joined the cast of “Zombie Reddy Nxt Lvl,” the sequel to the hit “Zombie Reddy,” in a powerhouse role, India’s People Media Factory has confirmed. The announcement, made on star Teja Sajja’s birthday, also confirms the film’s cast and creative team.
body: Suparn S. Varma, known for Prime Video’s “The Family Man” Season 2, Netflix’s “Rana Naidu” and film “Haq,” directs the sequel from a story created by Prasanth Varma. Gowra Hari, whose scores powered “HanuMan” and “Mirai,” composes the music.

Hussain Dalal, Prasanth Varma and Suparn S. Varma wrote the screenplay. T.G. Vishwa Prasad and Krithi Prasad produce for People Media Factory. The film will release in seven languages – Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Malayalam, Nepali and Japanese.

Suparn S. Varma said the goal was to surprise both himself and the audience with something unlike anything seen before. “Zombies have always been a fascinating expression of our worst catastrophes, and with this film, we wanted to take that idea to the next level,” he said. “We’ve taken the foundational brilliance that Prasanth Varma created and blown it wide open, building a never-seen-before zombieverse. It’s been an absolute treat to explore a genre with such enormous creative possibilities and collaborate with stalwarts who bring their own seasoned finesse to the film. Here’s wishing one of them – the audience’s superstar and favourite zombie slayer, Teja Sajja, a very happy birthday!”

articles.title: Drive-in cinemas are rare these days. But the last one in Melbourne’s north still draws a faithful crowd
articles.summary: The drive-in demands little of its audience. You can lie down, bring your dog and talk without fear of being hushed. Mridula Amin spent a night at one of the last of a dying breed. Between a funeral parlour and a sink factory, a queue of cars slowly disappears down a driveway.
body: “There’s something about watching a film under the stars, in the night air,” says Michael O’Neill, a car detailer who lives in Echuca, a five-hour return trip from the Coburg Drive-In.
At the peak of their popularity, there were more than 300 drive-in cinemas in Australia. Now, the Coburg Drive-In is the last one left within an hour of the Melbourne CBD.
O’Neil has been coming to the drive-in for 20 years, and when the light-up sign comes into view, it’s not unlike the feeling of coming home. He visits monthly.

People back home have often jeered, telling him it’s a waste of time. But O’Neill finds the traditional cinema experience lacklustre, “sat in a dark room, with phones buzzing and people talking”. He wants to live the drive-in experience while he can.

body: Dallas rapper BigXthaPlug has been arrested in the US state of Texas on charges of driving while intoxicated, possession of marijuana and illegal possession of a firearm.
Allen County Police confirmed to BBC Newsbeat the 28-year-old, whose real name is Xavier Landum, was stopped on Friday. He was held in Collin County Jail and later released.
Separately, he is on bail following an arrest on similar charges a year ago.

articles.title: Genetically Engineered Soldiers? Star Trek's Jem'Hadar Explained
articles.summary: The Jem'Hadar have a fascinating history in the Star Trek franchise. Here's what you need to know about this species of genetically engineered soldiers.
body: Welcome to Trekspertise, a series where we break down the technology, history, details, and decisions that make the Star Trek universe so complex — and so fun.
When the creators of "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine" (which we once called the best "Trek" series) were creating the show, they kind of overfilled their plate.

For one thing, the series took place on the titular space station in a distant part of the galaxy that was fraught with drama. The station orbits the planet Bajor, which was, until very recently, militarily occupied by the evil, Nazi-like Cardassians. Deep Space Nine was built by the Cardassians, inherited by the Bajorans, but run and staffed by Starfleet, who are present to oversee and smooth over reconstruction efforts.

Like the Federation, the Dominion is a consortium of various alien species — only evil. They rule with an iron fist and have their own military infrastructure to enforce their draconian laws. Most notably, they have their own specialized fighting force in the form of the Jem'Hadar, a slave species of ultra-aggressive reptilian soldiers. The Jem'Hadar are 100% genetically engineered.

articles.title: Davis 'grateful' for support over cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: The Office star was appearing at convention in London, less than two weeks after announcing her condition.
body: Actress Lucy Davis has told fans she is "grateful" for their support as she made an appearance at a London sci-fi convention, following the recent revelation she has incurable breast cancer.

Davis, who was on a panel to talk about her role in the 2004 zombie-comedy Shaun of the Dead, told an audience of hundreds of people about the interactions she had enjoyed with the film's fans during the event.

"It's like this whole second family you never knew you had, everyone is like a community, friendly, supportive of not only us but you guys and each other," she said. "We need a bit more niceness in the world, so I'm grateful."
It was the first time Davis had appeared at a public event since announcing on 11 August that she has stage four breast cancer.

articles.title: Prime Videos's Hit Thriller Quietly Changed a 23-Year-Old Franchise's Formula
articles.summary: Currently climbing the Prime Video streaming charts is the simply titled horror-thriller Wrong Turn. Ostensibly a straight slasher flick from the description and poster art, it actually takes more risks than one may expect, with multiple twists and an end credits sequence that's an essential part…
body: Wrong Turn (2003) was a modest hit in theaters, earning $29 million, but really took on a life of its own on home media, where its throwback The Hills Have Eyes - style inbred splatter thrills found a new generation of fans — and spawned a seven-film series. Viewers taken by the bloody thrills of the 2021 film should absolutely see where the series began — and can, today, with it streaming free over on Plex.

Director Rob Schmidt's 2003 slasher is part of the early 2000s studio-horror period when, for a time, it seemed like 1980s-style gore-for-gore's-sake was making a comeback. And coming out the same year as Platinum Dunes' stylish, grisly Texas Chain Saw Massacre remake and a year before Saw kicked off the so-called "torture porn" era, Wrong Turn itself was a throwback to an even less reputable slasher subgenre: inbred backwoods killers.
